title: On my way: participles of going and coming
goal: On the phone, tell Sēf you're leaving the office and on your way, and hear that his cousin is flying back to London
tip: A participle is a verb used like an adjective: it agrees (ṭāliʿ, ṭālʿa, ṭālʿīn) and takes mub, not ma. From a verb of going or coming it means 'on my way, about to': ana ṭāliʿ il-ḥīn 'I'm leaving now'; wild ʿammi rājiʿ Landan bāchir 'my cousin's going back to London tomorrow'.
grammar: Active participles I: going and coming verbs for now and soon (ṭāliʿ, rājiʿ, nāzil; recycle rāyiḥ, yāy)
dialogue: A
ألو، وينك؟ نحن في المول من ساعة!
alō, wēnak? niḥin fi l-mōl min sāʿa!
Hello, where are you? We've been at the mall for an hour!
B
آسف، أنا طالع من المكتب الحين
āsif, ana ṭāliʿ min il-maktab il-ḥīn
Sorry, I'm just leaving the office now.
A
يلا بسرعة! ولد عمي راجع لندن باكر الصبح
yalla b-surʿa! wild ʿammi rājiʿ Landan bāchir iṣ-ṣubḥ
Hurry up! My cousin's going back to London tomorrow morning.
B
والله؟ زين، أنا ياي بالمترو. ربع ساعة بس
wallāh? zēn, ana yāy bil-mitrō. rubʿ sāʿa bas
Really? OK, I'm coming on the metro. Just a quarter of an hour.
A
ماشي. نحن نازلين تحت عند المطاعم
māshi. niḥin nāzlīn taḥt ʿind il-maṭāʿim
OK. We're heading downstairs, to the restaurants.
B
زين عيل. وطيارته الساعة كم؟
zēn ʿayal. w ṭayyārtah is-sāʿa cham?
Fine then. And what time's his flight?
A
الساعة تسع. أول ما توصل، دق علي
is-sāʿa tisʿ. awwal ma tōṣal, digg ʿalay
At nine. Ring me as soon as you get here.
items: I'm leaving, I'm heading out (said by a man)
a woman says: ana ṭālʿa (أنا طالعة); ana ṭāliʿ il-ḥīn = I'm just leaving
going back, on his way back; (he's) back (a man)
a woman: rājʿa (راجعة); a group: rājʿīn (راجعين)
going down, heading downstairs (a group, or 'we')
one man: nāzil (نازل); one woman: nāzla (نازلة)
ring me, give me a call (to a man)
to a woman: diggi ʿalay (دقي علي)
for an hour (now); an hour ago
like min yōmēn: for two days (now)
half an hour: nuṣṣ sāʿa (نص ساعة)
my flight: ṭayyārti (طيارتي); the plane: iṭ-ṭayyāra (الطيارة)
counting: tisʿa (تسعة); at seven: is-sāʿa sabʿ

title: Flying tonight: participles for plans
goal: At the office, ask Maryam about her trip, say you're not going away, and wish her a safe journey
tip: A participle with a time word is a plan: msāfir il-lēla 'flying tonight'. It agrees with the person: msāfir (a man), msāfra (a woman), msāfrīn (a group, or 'we'). For 'not', use mub: mub msāfir 'I'm not going away'.
grammar: Active participles II: plans and the near future, with the -a and -īn forms (msāfra, rāyḥīn, mub msāfir)
culture: Someone setting off on a trip is wished tōṣal bis-salāma (to a woman tōṣalīn), 'may you arrive safely', and answers allāh ysallmak. When they come back, greet them with il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma.
dialogue: B
صباح الخير مريم. شو هالشنطة؟ مسافرة؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr Maryam. shu hash-shanṭa? msāfra?
Good morning, Maryam. What's with the bag? Are you going away?
A
صباح النور. هيه، مسافرين الليلة، أنا وأهلي
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē, msāfrīn il-lēla, ana w ahli
Good morning. Yes, we're flying tonight, my family and I.
B
ما شاء الله! وين رايحين؟
mā shāʼ allāh! wēn rāyḥīn?
How lovely! Where are you going?
A
صلالة، عند خالتي. وانت؟ مسافر في الإجازة؟
Ṣalāla, ʿind khālti. w inta? msāfir fi l-ijāza?
Salalah, to my aunt's. And you? Are you going away for the holiday?
B
لا، مب مسافر. أهلي يايين دبي. وانتي متى راجعة؟
la, mub msāfir. ahli yāyīn Dbayy. w inti mita rājʿa?
No, I'm not going away. My family's coming to Dubai. And when are you back?
A
يوم الأحد إن شاء الله. سلم لي على أهلك!
yōm il-aḥad in shāʼ allāh. sallim-li ʿala ahlak!
On Sunday, God willing. Give my regards to your family!
B
إن شاء الله. توصلين بالسلامة!
in shāʼ allāh. tōṣalīn bis-salāma!
I will. Have a safe trip!
A
الله يسلمك. مع السلامة
allāh ysallmak. maʿa s-salāma
Thank you. Bye.
items: are you going away? are you travelling? (to a woman)
where are you going? (to a group)
to one man: wēn rāyiḥ? (وين رايح؟); to one woman: wēn rāyḥa? (وين رايحة؟)
at my father's sister's: ʿind ʿammti (عند عمتي)
I'm not going away, I'm not travelling (said by a man)
a woman says: mub msāfra (مب مسافرة)
when are you back? (to a woman)
to a man: mita rājiʿ? (متى راجع؟)
have a safe trip (to a woman; lit. may you arrive safely)
to a man: tōṣal bis-salāma (توصل بالسلامة); reply: allāh ysallmak, to a woman allāh ysallmich
on holiday, for the holiday, in the break

title: Do you know where it is? ʿārif, fāhim, shāyif
goal: In a university corridor, ask Sēf what he knows and can see, using the participles ʿārif, fāhim and shāyif
tip: From verbs of knowing and seeing, the participle is a state right now: ʿārif 'I know', fāhim 'I understand', shāyif 'I can see'. Negate it with mub: mub ʿārif 'I don't know'. Your ma aʿarf and ma adri still say the same thing.
grammar: Active participles III: knowing and seeing verbs for a present state (ʿārif, fāhim, shāyif)
dialogue: B
سيف، انت عارف وين المحاضرة اليوم؟
Sēf, inta ʿārif wēn il-muḥāẓra l-yōm?
Sēf, do you know where the lecture is today?
A
لا، مب عارف. بس شايف هذاك الريّال؟
la, mub ʿārif. bas shāyif hādhāk ir-rayyāl?
No, I don't. But do you see that man?
B
هيه، شايفه. منو هو؟
hē, shāyfah. minu huwa?
Yes, I can see him. Who is he?
A
هذا الدكتور اليديد حقنا. هو عارف كل شي
hādha d-daktōr il-yidīd ḥaggna. huwa ʿārif kill shay
That's our new lecturer. He knows everything.
B
زين، بسأله. بس ترا أنا مب فاهم المادة
zēn, basʼalah. bas tara ana mub fāhim il-māda
OK, I'll ask him. But mind you, I don't understand the module.
A
عادي، محد فاهم شي! حتى أنا
ʿādi, maḥḥad fāhim shay! ḥatta ana
Don't worry, nobody understands a thing! Me included.
B
عيل خلنا نذاكر ويا بعض
ʿayal khallna ndhākir wiyya baʿaẓ
Then let's revise together.
A
فكرة حلوة. بس انت عارف، أنا كسلان!
fikra ḥilwa. bas inta ʿārif, ana kaslān!
Good idea. But you know I'm lazy!
items: to a woman: inti ʿārfa? (انتي عارفة؟)
I don't know (said by a man)
a woman says: mub ʿārfa (مب عارفة); ma aʿarf and ma adri mean the same
(can) see, seeing; do you see? (a man)
a woman: shāyfa (شايفة); shāyfah = I can see him
maḥḥad fāhim shay = nobody understands a thing
even me, me included; me neither (after a negative)
we revise, let's revise (for an exam)

title: I've already eaten: participles for what's done
goal: At Bū Rāshid's majlis, say politely that you've already had dinner, accept a little, and tell him you've passed your exams
tip: From verbs of doing, the participle says something is done and still true now: ana mitʿashshi 'I've (already) had dinner', il-ahal msawwīn harīs 'the family have made harees', nājiḥ '(I've) passed'. It agrees like an adjective: msawwi, msawwya, msawwīn.
grammar: Active participles IV: doing verbs for a finished action (mitʿashshi, msawwi, nājiḥ)
culture: A host keeps offering food, and a guest who has already eaten can say ana mitʿashshi once, then accept a little. Older men often say il-ahal, 'the family', for the people at home rather than naming their wife.
dialogue: A
حياك الله يا ولدي. تفضل، العشا جاهز
ḥayyāk allāh yā wildi. tfaẓẓal, il-ʿasha jāhiz
Welcome, son. Come in, dinner's ready.
B
الله يحييك يا عمي. بس والله أنا متعشي
allāh yḥayyīk yā ʿammi. bas wallāh ana mitʿashshi
Thank you, uncle. But honestly, I've already had dinner.
A
متعشي؟ ما يصير! الأهل مسوين هريس عشانك
mitʿashshi? ma yṣīr! il-ahal msawwīn harīs ʿashānak
Had dinner? That won't do! The family have made harees for you.
B
ما قصرت يا عمي. بس شوي، أنا شبعان
mā gaṣṣart yā ʿammi. bas shwayy, ana shabʿān
That's very kind, uncle. Just a little, then; I'm full.
A
ما سوينا شي. وشو مسوي في الامتحانات؟
mā sawwēna shay. w shu msawwi fi l-imtiḥānāt?
It was nothing. And how have you done in your exams?
B
الحمد لله، ناجح في كل المواد
il-ḥamdu lillāh, nājiḥ fi kill il-mawādd
Thank God, I've passed all my modules.
A
ما شاء الله عليك! وسيف؟ شو مسوي؟
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! w Sēf? shu msawwi?
Well done! And Sēf? How has he done?
B
سيف بعد ناجح. وهو ياي الحين
Sēf baʿad nājiḥ. w huwa yāy il-ḥīn
Sēf's passed too. And he's on his way now.
items: I've (already) had dinner (said by a man)
a woman says: ana mitʿashshya (أنا متعشية); had lunch: mitghaddi (متغدي)
have made, have done (a group, or 'we')
one man: msawwi (مسوي); one woman: msawwya (مسوية)
how have you done? what have you been up to? (to a man)
to a woman: shu msawwya? (شو مسوية؟)
in all the modules, in every subject
lunch is ready: il-ghada jāhiz (الغدا جاهز)
the family, the people at home

title: Still in bed! nāyim, ṣāḥi, wāgif
goal: Phone Sēf, who has overslept, while you and Fahad wait outside, using participles for the state someone is in
tip: Some participles describe the state someone is in: nāyim 'asleep, in bed', ṣāḥi 'awake', wāgif 'standing'. There's no word for 'is': ana lil-ḥīn nāyim 'I'm still in bed', niḥin wāgfīn barra 'we're standing outside'.
grammar: Active participles V: states (nāyim, ṣāḥi, wāgif); no 'is' before them
dialogue: B
ألو سيف؟ وينك؟ أنا وفهد واقفين برا
alō Sēf? wēnak? ana w Fahad wāgfīn barra
Hello, Sēf? Where are you? Fahad and I are standing outside.
A
آسف يا ريّال! أنا للحين نايم
āsif yā rayyāl! ana lil-ḥīn nāyim
Sorry, mate! I'm still in bed.
B
نايم؟! صار لنا ساعة نترياك!
nāyim?! ṣār-lna sāʿa nitrayyāk!
In bed?! We've been waiting for you for an hour!
A
سهرت لين الصبح. انتو تغديتوا؟
sihart lēn iṣ-ṣubḥ. intu tghaddētu?
I was up till morning. Have you had lunch?
B
لا، للحين ما تغدينا. وفهد يوعان وايد!
la, lil-ḥīn ma tghaddēna. w Fahad yōʿān wāyid!
No, we haven't had lunch yet. And Fahad's really hungry!
A
زين، أنا نازل الحين. خمس دقايق بس
zēn, ana nāzil il-ḥīn. khams dagāyig bas
OK, I'm coming down now. Just five minutes.
B
زين، بس لا تنام مرة ثانية!
zēn, bas la tnām marra thānya!
OK, but don't go back to sleep!
A
لا تحاتي، أنا صاحي الحين والله!
la tḥāti, ana ṣāḥi l-ḥīn wallāh!
Don't worry, I'm awake now, honestly!
items: a woman: nāyma (نايمة); a group: nāymīn (نايمين)
one man: wāgif (واقف); one woman: wāgfa (واقفة)
we've been (here) for an hour, it's been an hour (for us)
for me: ṣār-li sāʿa (صار لي ساعة)
I stayed up late; you stayed up late (to a man)
have you had lunch? (to a group)
to one man: tghaddēt? (تغديت؟); to one woman: tghaddēti? (تغديتي؟)
we haven't had lunch, we didn't have lunch
I haven't had lunch: ma tghaddēt (ما تغديت)
I'm coming down, I'm on my way down (said by a man)
a woman says: ana nāzla (أنا نازلة)

title: A weekend in Hatta: participles with a group
goal: Ask Sēf and Fahad about the weekend trip to Hatta: what they've booked, who's bringing what, when they set off
tip: With a group, the participle takes -īn: rāyḥīn, ṭālʿīn, ḥājzīn. From a doing verb, it's done: ḥājzīn il-fundug 'we've booked the hotel'; Fahad mākhidh ijāza 'Fahad has taken time off'. From a going verb, it's the plan: ṭālʿīn baʿd ṣalāt il-fajr 'we're leaving after dawn prayer'.
grammar: Active participles VI: the group form -īn, and done vs planned (ḥājzīn, mākhidh, ṭālʿīn)
culture: In the cooler months, many people in the UAE head out of the city at weekends: to the mountains, the desert or a camp. Trips often start early, after the dawn prayer, to make the most of the day. Nights out of town can be cold, so take a jacket.
dialogue: B
يا شباب، انتو رايحين حتا يوم الخميس؟
yā shabāb, intu rāyḥīn Ḥatta yōm il-khamīs?
Guys, are you going to Hatta on Thursday?
A
هيه، رايحين. وانت ياي ويانا، صح؟
hē, rāyḥīn. w inta yāy wiyyāna, ṣaḥḥ?
Yes, we are. And you're coming with us, right?
B
إن شاء الله. انتو حاجزين الفندق؟
in shāʼ allāh. intu ḥājzīn il-fundug?
God willing. Have you booked the hotel?
A
حاجزين من أسبوع. وفهد ماخذ إجازة يومين
ḥājzīn min usbūʿ. w Fahad mākhidh ijāza yōmēn
We booked it a week ago. And Fahad's taken two days off.
B
حلو! أييب شي وياي؟
ḥilu! ayīb shay wiyyāy?
Great! Shall I bring anything?
A
لا، فهد يايب كل شي. بس لا تنسى الجاكيت
la, Fahad yāyib kill shay. bas la tinsa l-jākēt
No, Fahad's bringing everything. Just don't forget your jacket.
B
ماشي. انتو طالعين الساعة كم؟
māshi. intu ṭālʿīn is-sāʿa cham?
OK. What time are you setting off?
A
طالعين بعد صلاة الفجر. لا تكون نايم!
ṭālʿīn baʿd ṣalāt il-fajr. la tkūn nāyim!
We're leaving after the dawn prayer. Don't oversleep!
items: one man: ḥājiz (حاجز); one woman: ḥājza (حاجزة)
(has) taken time off, (is) on leave (a man)
a woman: yāyba (يايبة); a group: yāybīn (يايبين); you'll see written جايب
one man: ṭāliʿ (طالع); one woman: ṭālʿa (طالعة)
a week ago; for a week (now)
after the dawn prayer, at first light
two days off, two days' leave
a week off: ijāza usbūʿ (إجازة أسبوع)
la tkūn nāyim = don't be asleep; to a woman: la tkūnīn (لا تكونين)

title: I was driving: kint gāʿid
goal: Explain to Sēf why you missed his calls last night, saying what you were doing at the time
tip: Put kān before gāʿid and the -ing moves into the past: kint gāʿid asūg 'I was driving'. kān changes like any past verb (kint, kān, kānat, kinna, kānaw), and gāʿid agrees too: kinna gāʿdīn nākil 'we were eating'. kān + a state works the same way: kint nāyim 'I was asleep'.
grammar: Past progressive: kān gāʿid + present verb 'was …-ing'; kān + participle (kint nāyim)
dialogue: A
وينك البارحة؟ دقيت عليك ثلاث مرات!
wēnak il-bārḥa? daggēt ʿalēk thalāth marrāt!
Where were you last night? I rang you three times!
B
آسف، كنت قاعد أسوق. ما سمعت التلفون
āsif, kint gāʿid asūg. ma simaʿt it-tilifōn
Sorry, I was driving. I didn't hear the phone.
A
وبعدين؟ دقيت مرة ثانية الساعة تسع
w baʿdēn? daggēt marra thānya s-sāʿa tisʿ
And after that? I rang again at nine.
B
الساعة تسع كنا قاعدين ناكل في المطعم
is-sāʿa tisiʿ kinna gāʿdīn nākil fi l-maṭʿam
At nine we were eating at the restaurant.
A
ويا منو؟ ليش ما قلت لي؟
wiyya minu? lēsh ma gilt-li?
Who with? Why didn't you tell me?
B
ويا الجماعة من الشغل. وبعدها كنت نايم
wiyya l-jamāʿa min ish-shughul. w baʿd-ha kint nāyim
With the people from work. And after that I was asleep.
A
ترا كنت قاعد أترياك عشان المباراة!
tara kint gāʿid atrayyāk ʿashān il-mubārā!
I was waiting for you for the match, you know!
B
آسف والله. المرة الياية بشوفها وياك
āsif wallāh. il-marra l-yāya bashūfha wiyyāk
I'm really sorry. Next time I'll watch it with you.
items: I was (…-ing); you were (…-ing) (to a man)
a woman says: kint gāʿda (كنت قاعدة); to a woman: kinti gāʿda (كنتي قاعدة); + a present verb: kint gāʿid asūg
kinna gāʿdīn nākil = we were eating
I was asleep; you were asleep (to a man)
a woman says: kint nāyma (كنت نايمة); to a woman: kinti nāyma (كنتي نايمة)
I rang you, I called you (to a man)
to a woman: daggēt ʿalēch (دقيت عليج)
I didn't hear; you didn't hear (to a man)
to a woman: ma simaʿti (ما سمعتي)
(I'm) waiting for you (after gāʿid); shall I wait for you? (to a man) (UAE)
to a woman: atrayyāch (أترياج); I'll wait for you: batrayyāk (بترياك)

title: What were you doing? kān gāʿid for he, she and they
goal: At the office, hear Maryam's story about yesterday's meeting and ask her what she was doing
tip: kān gāʿid works for every person; both words agree: il-mudīr kān gāʿid yitkallam 'the manager was talking', kint gāʿda aktib 'I was writing (a woman)', kānaw gāʿdīn yṭālʿūnah 'they were staring at him'. To a woman: shu kinti gāʿda tsawwīn? 'what were you doing?'
grammar: Past progressive II: kān gāʿid for every person (kān, kānat, kinti, kānaw gāʿdīn)
culture: A Gulf story often opens with simaʿt shu ṣār? 'did you hear what happened?', and the listener keeps it going with w baʿdēn? 'and then?'. Saying maskīn 'poor guy' about someone shows sympathy, not mockery.
dialogue: A
سمعت شو صار أمس في الاجتماع؟
simaʿt shu ṣār ams fi l-ijtimāʿ?
Did you hear what happened in the meeting yesterday?
B
لا، كنت قاعد أذاكر في الجامعة. شو صار؟
la, kint gāʿid adhākir fi l-jāmʿa. shu ṣār?
No, I was revising at university. What happened?
A
المدير كان قاعد يتكلم عن المشروع
il-mudīr kān gāʿid yitkallam ʿan il-mashrūʿ
The manager was talking about the project.
B
إي، وانتي؟ شو كنتي قاعدة تسوين؟
ī, w inti? shu kinti gāʿda tsawwīn?
Right, and you? What were you doing?
A
كنت قاعدة أكتب. والموظف اليديد كان نايم!
kint gāʿda aktib. w il-muwaẓẓaf il-yidīd kān nāyim!
I was taking notes. And the new guy was asleep!
B
نايم؟! والمدير شافه؟
nāyim?! w il-mudīr shāfah?
Asleep?! And did the manager see him?
A
هيه! وكلهم كانوا قاعدين يطالعونه
hē! w killhum kānaw gāʿdīn yṭālʿūnah
Yes! And they were all staring at him.
B
مسكين! أكيد كان تعبان
maskīn! akīd kān taʿbān
Poor guy! He must have been tired.
items: she was (…-ing): kānat gāʿda (كانت قاعدة); kān gāʿid yitkallam = he was talking
to a man: kint gāʿid (كنت قاعد)
did you hear what happened? (to a man)
to a woman: simaʿti shu ṣār? (سمعتي شو صار؟)
she talks about: titkallam ʿan (تتكلم عن)
the new employee, the new guy at work
he saw him, he saw it (m.)
(they're) looking at him, staring at him

title: Everyone started laughing: gām + verb
goal: Tell Sēf a funny thing that happened on the metro, using gām for what people suddenly started doing
tip: gām 'he got up' + a present verb means 'he started to, he suddenly began': gām yiẓḥak 'he burst out laughing'. gām is a past verb and agrees, and so does the verb after it: gāmat tiẓḥak 'she started laughing', gimna niẓḥak 'we started laughing'.
grammar: Inceptive gām + present verb 'started to' (gām yiẓḥak, gāmat tiẓḥak, gimna niẓḥak)
dialogue: A
شفيك تضحك؟ شو صار؟
shfīk tiẓḥak? shu ṣār?
What are you laughing at? What happened?
B
كنت قاعد في المترو، وريّال نايم يمي
kint gāʿid fi l-mitrō, w rayyāl nāyim yammi
I was sitting on the metro, and a man was asleep next to me.
A
زين، وبعدين؟ شو سوى؟
zēn, w baʿdēn? shu sawwa?
OK, and then? What did he do?
B
دق تلفونه، وقام يتكلم بصوت عالي
dagg tilifōnah, w gām yitkallam b-ṣōt ʿāli
His phone rang, and he started talking loudly.
A
في المترو؟! والناس شو سووا؟
fi l-mitrō?! w in-nās shu sawwaw?
On the metro?! And what did people do?
B
الكل قام يطالعه، وبنت صغيرة قامت تضحك
il-kill gām yṭālʿah, w bint ṣghīra gāmat tiẓḥak
Everyone started staring at him, and a little girl started laughing.
A
وانت؟ قمت تضحك بعد؟
w inta? gimt tiẓḥak baʿad?
And you? Did you start laughing too?
B
هيه، وقمنا كلنا نضحك! حتى هو
hē, w gimna killna niẓḥak! ḥatta huwa
Yes, and we all started laughing! Even him.
items: he started laughing, he burst out laughing
she started laughing: gāmat tiẓḥak (قامت تضحك)
I started (+ a verb); you started (to a man); also: I got up
to a woman: gimti (قمتي); gimt aẓḥak = I started laughing
we started (+ a verb); we got up
what are you laughing at? (to a man)
to a woman: shfīch tiẓḥakīn? (شفيج تضحكين؟)
my phone rang: dagg tilifōni (دق تلفوني)
il-kill gām = everyone started; wēn il-kill? = where's everyone?
a little boy: walad ṣghīr (ولد صغير)
what did he do? shu sawwa? (شو سوى؟)

title: I was going to call you: kint b- + verb
goal: Turn up late to dinner with Sēf and Fahad, apologise to the group and say what you were going to do
tip: kān + b- + a present verb is 'was going to, was about to': kint bagūl-lak 'I was going to tell you', kinna binrūḥ 'we were about to go', kān biyrūḥ 'he was about to go'. kān agrees, and so does the verb after b-. Kuwaitis say this too, and also use rāḥ: kint rāḥ agūl-lak.
grammar: 'Was going to': kān + b- + present verb (kint bagūl-lak, kinna binrūḥ); Kuwait: kān rāḥ
culture: Saying il-ʿasha ʿala ḥsābi 'dinner's on me' is a friendly way to make up for keeping friends waiting. Friends often argue over who pays (khallha ʿalay! la wallāh!): an offer is usually turned down once before it's accepted, so expect to insist.
dialogue: A
وينك يا ريّال؟ كنا بنروح!
wēnak yā rayyāl? kinna binrūḥ!
Where have you been, mate? We were about to go!
B
آسف يا شباب! كنت بتصل فيكم، بس نسيت تلفوني
āsif yā shabāb! kint battaṣil fīkum, bas nisēt tilifōni
Sorry, guys! I was going to call you, but I forgot my phone.
A
نسيته وين؟ في البيت؟
nisētah wēn? fi l-bēt?
Forgot it where? At home?
B
هيه، في البيت. كنت مستعيل وايد
hē, fi l-bēt. kint mistaʿyil wāyid
Yes, at home. I was in a real hurry.
A
ترا كنت بقول لك: فهد زعلان منك
tara kint bagūl-lak: Fahad zaʿlān minnak
I was going to tell you: Fahad's cross with you.
B
ليش زعلان؟ شو سويت له؟
lēsh zaʿlān? shu sawwēt-lah?
Why's he cross? What have I done to him?
A
ولا شي، بس يوعان. كان بيروح البيت!
wala shay, bas yōʿān. kān biyrūḥ il-bēt!
Nothing, he's just hungry. He was about to go home!
B
يلا نطلب عيل! والعشا على حسابي
yalla niṭlub ʿayal! w il-ʿasha ʿala ḥsābi
Let's order, then! And dinner's on me.
items: I was going to tell you (to a man)
to a woman: kint bagūl-lich (كنت بقول لج); Kuwait: kint rāḥ agūl-lak (كنت راح أقول لك)
I was going to call you (to a group)
to one man: kint battaṣil fīk (كنت بتصل فيك); to one woman: kint battaṣil fīch (كنت بتصل فيج)
we were about to go, we were going to go
Kuwait: kinna rāḥ nrūḥ (كنا راح نروح)
he was about to go, he was going to go
she was about to go: kānat bitrūḥ (كانت بتروح)
a woman: mistaʿyla (مستعيلة); you'll see written مستعجل
I forgot my phone, I left my phone behind
you forgot your phone: nisēt tilifōnak (نسيت تلفونك) to a man, nisēti tilifōnich (نسيتي تلفونج) to a woman
I forgot it (m.), I left it (behind); you forgot it (to a man)
to a woman: nisētīh (نسيتيه); a feminine thing: nisēt-ha (نسيتها)
cross with you, upset with you (to a man)
with you (to a woman): zaʿlān minnich (زعلان منج); a woman who's cross: zaʿlāna minnak
what have I done to him? what did you do to him? (to a man)
to a woman: shu sawwētī-lah? (شو سويتي له؟); to her: shu sawwēt-lha? (شو سويت لها؟)

title: A camel in the road: telling what happened
goal: Tell Bū Rāshid about a scare on the road back from Hatta: what you were doing, what happened, what nearly happened
tip: A short story uses this block's three tools: the background with kān gāʿid (Sēf kān gāʿid ysūg 'Sēf was driving'), a sudden turn with gām (gām yṣārikh 'he started shouting') and what nearly happened with kint b- (kint bamūt min il-khōf 'I nearly died of fright').
grammar: Telling an incident: kān gāʿid for the background, gām for a sudden turn, kint b- for what nearly happened
culture: Outside the cities, camels sometimes wander onto the road, above all at night, so drive slowly there. Someone back from a trip is welcomed with il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma; il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala salāmatkum is also said when people have had a scare. The answer to both is allāh ysallmak.
dialogue: A
الحمد لله على السلامة يا ولدي. كيف كانت حتا؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma yā wildi. chēf kānat Ḥatta?
Welcome back, son. How was Hatta?
B
الله يسلمك يا عمي. حلوة، بس صار لنا شي غريب
allāh ysallmak yā ʿammi. ḥilwa, bas ṣār-lna shay gharīb
Thank you, uncle. Lovely, but something strange happened to us.
A
خير إن شاء الله؟ شو صار؟
khēr in shāʼ allāh? shu ṣār?
Nothing bad, I hope? What happened?
B
كنا راجعين بالليل، وسيف كان قاعد يسوق
kinna rājʿīn bil-lēl, w Sēf kān gāʿid ysūg
We were on our way back at night, and Sēf was driving.
A
زين، وبعدين يا ولدي؟
zēn, w baʿdēn yā wildi?
Yes, and then, son?
B
بعير واقف في نص الشارع! وسيف قام يصارخ
biʿīr wāgif fi nuṣṣ ish-shāriʿ! w Sēf gām yṣārikh
A camel standing in the middle of the road! And Sēf started shouting.
A
الحمد لله على سلامتكم! أكيد كنت خايف
il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala salāmatkum! akīd kint khāyif
Thank God you're all safe! You must have been scared.
B
الله يسلمك. كنت بموت من الخوف! ومن يومها سيف يسوق شوي شوي
allāh ysallmak. kint bamūt min il-khōf! w min yōmha Sēf ysūg shwayy shwayy
Thank you. I nearly died of fright! And ever since, Sēf drives slowly.
items: how was it (f.)? how did it go?
about a masculine thing: chēf kān? (كيف كان؟)
nothing bad, I hope? is everything all right?
in the middle of the road
to one man: il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala salāmtak (على سلامتك)
I nearly died of fright (lit. I was going to die of fear)
